text:
eva_support: Customer reported 503s from their app after we migrated their tenant to new VPCs. They say internal service endpoint resolves to NXDOMAIN intermittently and TLS handshake fails to downstream svc.

matt_sre: can you paste the error they see? 503 from our API or downstream?

eva_support: They see our API return 503 with logs showing `upstream connect error or connection refused`. App-level curl to the service endpoint shows `curl: (7) Failed to connect` sometimes, and sometimes `curl: (6) Could not resolve host`.

sam_platform: likely DNS or node-local cache. Any changes to resolver rules or hosted zone associations during the migration?

eva_support: They had a Route53 private hosted zone moved between accounts and we also updated resolver rules last night. Customer timeline: migration at 02:10 UTC, errors started ~02:12 and are still happening.

matt_sre: can you ask for a `dig +trace` and `dig @169.254.20.10` (nodelocal) output from a pod in the tenant VPC? also the node-local-resolver IP for us is `169.254.20.10` in our env.

eva_support: got this from their pod (redacted):

```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> svc.priv.example.internal +short
; global options: +cmd
NXDOMAIN

; dig @169.254.20.10 svc.priv.example.internal +short
REFUSED

;; Query time: 2 msec
;; SERVER: 169.254.20.10#53(169.254.20.10)
```

matt_sre: REFUSED from node-local resolver is telling — either the node-local daemon dropped the request or iptables blocked forwarding from pod to node-local. Do they have egress allowlist for UDP/53 to the resolver IP?

sam_platform: also check whether the VPC association for the private hosted zone exists for that VPC. If the hosted zone moved accounts, the assoc could be missing -> NXDOMAIN at upstream. But REFUSED at node-local suggests local component.

eva_support: i asked them to run `kubectl exec -ti pod -- nslookup svc.priv.example.internal 169.254.20.10` and they got `;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached` on some nodes and `REFUSED` on others.

matt_sre: sounds like node-local caches in some nodes are unhappy. Could be crashloop or config changed at rollout. Any recent DaemonSet image updates for `nodelocal-dns`? deploy-bot: Deployment event: nodelocal-dns daemonset rollout completed 02:00 UTC - image: `nodelocal:v1.4.2` -> `v1.4.3`.

sam_platform: that rollout time matches. If v1.4.3 has stricter ACLs or changed bind address, pods might refuse queries from certain ranges. Ask for `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide` and `kubectl logs` for node-local on a node that returns REFUSED.

eva_support: they attached logs snippet from node-local: `E: failed to load policy: /etc/nodelocal/acl.conf: permission denied`.

matt_sre: aha. ACL misconfigured or file permissions wrong after image change. Node-local then serves REFUSED. Quick mitigation: restart daemonset with old image `v1.4.2` or remove ACL until config fixed.

sam_platform: also confirm Route53 zone assoc: `aws route53 get-hosted-zone --id ZXXXXXXXX` shows associations include the tenant VPC. If assoc missing, even fixed node-local will still NXDOMAIN.

eva_support: customer ran `aws route53 list-hosted-zones-by-vpc --vpc-id vpc-0abc123` -> returns the hosted zone present. So assoc is fine.

matt_sre: good — primary issue is node-local refusing due to ACL/permission error after daemonset update. Steps to remediate: 1) roll daemonset back to `v1.4.2` (controls immediate availability) 2) fix file permissions on ACL in image or ConfigMap and roll forward 3) verify with `dig @169.254.20.10 svc.priv.example.internal +short` 4) after DNS stable, test TLS handshake: `openssl s_client -connect svc.priv.example.internal:443 -servername svc.priv.example.internal` to ensure cert SNI ok.

eva_support: customer applied rollback to v1.4.2 and DNS resolved consistently again. TLS handshakes now succeed. They still want root cause; i'll open follow-up with ops to inspect the v1.4.3 image change and how ACL file permission got stricter during build.

sam_platform: also recommend adding a small healthcheck for node-local that checks `dig @127.0.0.1` and `dig @169.254.20.10` so we catch REFUSED quickly during future rollouts.

matt_sre: agreed. I'll add a runbook snippet: 1) if REFUSED from node-local -> check daemonset image and ConfigMap ACL; 2) check iptables/nft rules for -A KUBE-... that might block pod->node traffic; 3) verify hosted zone associations as a separate step.

eva_support: thanks all — I'll mark as resolved with workaround and escalate to infra for image fix. :thumbsup:
